children: New Delhi, Nov. 4 -- BLS Polymers share price extended their winning streak for a second consecutive session on Wednesday, 4 November, rising nearly 7% to hit a fresh record high of Rs.288 apiece on the BSE. The stock has surged around 92% over its IPO price of Rs.150, following an impressive market debut on Tuesday.

The stock had listed at a substantial premium on 3 November, closing nearly 79.5% above its issue price. On the BSE, BLS Polymers shares opened at Rs.244.10, marking a gain of 62.73% over the IPO price. Buying interest intensified during the session, taking the stock to an intraday high of Rs.285.25, up 90.16%. It eventually settled at Rs.269.30, a premium of 79.53%.

On the NSE, the shares debuted at Rs.248, representing a 65.33% premium over the issue price, and closed at Rs.268.80, up 79.2%. The company commanded a market capitalisation of Rs.1,670.52 crore at the close of its listing day session.

The company's Rs.255-crore initial public offering (IPO) witnessed overwhelming investor demand, with the issue subscribed 241.22 times on the final day of bidding on Thursday. The IPO was entirely a fresh issue of 1.7 crore equity shares, with the price band fixed at Rs.142-150 per share.

According to the red herring prospectus, BLS Polymers plans to deploy Rs.77.56 crore from the IPO proceeds to expand its manufacturing facility and increase production capacity for select existing products. Another Rs.89.5 crore has been earmarked for working capital requirements, while the remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
BLS Polymers manufactures custom-formulated polymer compounds used across industries such as telecommunications, power, railways, water infrastructure, and oil and gas distribution.

The company operates a manufacturing facility in Goa with an installed capacity of 35,251 metric tonnes per annum. Its distribution network spans 23 states and Union Territories in India, while its exports reach 13 countries, including the US, Germany, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Bangladesh.

Dr. Ravi Singh, Chief Research Officer at Master Capital Services Ltd, said BLS Polymers made a strong debut on the Indian stock market, listing at Rs.248 on the NSE, a premium of 65.33% over its issue price of Rs.150.

Incorporated in 1991 and headquartered in New Delhi, BLS Polymers manufactures custom-formulated polymer compounds for critical industries such as telecommunications, power, railways, water infrastructure, and oil and gas distribution. Its diversified product portfolio includes high-density polyethylene (HDPE), medium-density polyethylene (MDPE), linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE), cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE), halogen-free flame-retardant (HFFR), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), cable-filling and adhesive-coating compounds. These products are used in insulation, sheathing, jacketing and corrosion protection applications for wires, cables and underground pipelines.

The company operates a manufacturing facility spread across approximately 24,220 square metres in Goa, equipped with 11 manufacturing machines and an in-house quality control laboratory. Its revenue from operations increased to Rs.349.43 crore in FY26, while its EBITDA margin improved to 13.33% from 12.08% in the previous year.

Highlighting the industry's growth prospects, Singh noted that the Indian polymer compounding market expanded from $6 billion in 2019 to $9.9 billion in 2025. It is projected to reach $16.5 billion by 2031, registering a CAGR of around 9% between 2026 and 2031.

According to Singh, investors should closely monitor the company's ability to sustain revenue growth, improve profitability and execute its planned capacity expansion while maintaining healthy cash flows. Key parameters to track include quarterly revenue performance, EBITDA margins, capacity utilisation and cash flows, along with demand trends for polymer compounds used in wires, cables and industrial pipelines.
